content.title: HBO Max | With the Standard and Premium plans, you can watch select live events, including MLB, NHL, NCAA Men's March Madness, and U.S. Soccer.
content.text: Sports on HBO Max Sports on HBO Max is the place for premium sports content, including more than 1,700 live events. Watch select live events, including MLB, NHL, NCAA Men's March Madness, U.S. Soccer, and premier cycling events on HBO Max. Live Sports is included with the Standard and Premium plans. Plan availability varies by subscription provider. For more info, go to HBO Max plans. In HBO Max, choose Sports (top of screen or left edge on TVs). Here you'll find live games, upcoming games, and highlights from recent games. You can also find games scheduled for the next 2 weeks using our Digital Assistant Sports Schedule. Sports Q&A What is Sports on HBO Max? Sports on HBO Max is the place for premium sports content, including more than 1,700 live events. In addition to live sports, Sports on HBO Max includes pre- and post-game studio programming, multi-sport on-demand content, special features, and live series from Bleacher Report (e.g. live coverage of the NFL Draft, popular vodcasts and the Creator League). What live sports can I watch? In HBO Max, choose Sports (top of screen or left edge on TVs). Here you'll find live and upcoming games. With Sports on HBO Max, you can stream live games, matches, and events in 2026, including: MLB: 2026 MLB regular season coverage starting in April 2026, featuring a weekly Tuesday Night game throughout the season. NASCAR: Exclusive coverage of NASCAR's inaugural five race In-Season Tournament starting June 2026, as well as all practices and qualifiers for Summer and Fall races and exclusive in-car camera and audio for all races all season long. Note Full race coverage is only available for select NASCAR events on HBO Max. NCAA Big 12 and Big East: College basketball and college football regular season (select games). NCAA College Football Playoffs: 2 first round games of 2026 playoffs. NCAA March Madness®: A selection of 2026 March Madness® games. For more info, go to 2026 NCAA March Madness® on HBO Max. NHL: 2026 regular season (select games), select games from the inaugural 4 Nations Face-Off, the 2026 NHL Stanley Cup Playoffs (select games) and the 2026 NHL Stanley Cup Final. Roland-Garros: More than 900 matches, including the Men's Singles and Women's Singles Championships. T100: Coverage of 8 races around the globe and the inaugural T100 Grand Final at the end of November. Unrivaled: More than 45 games of Unrivaled's inaugural season of 3x3 women's basketball, starting January 2026. WEC: All 8 rounds of the 2026 World Endurance Championship, including the legendary 24 Hours of Le Mans. Cycling: Over 300 live racing events across road, mountain bike, track, BMX, and cyclocross. Players Era Festival, expanding to an 18-team field in 2026. English-language live coverage of U.S. Men's National Soccer Team and U.S. Women's National Soccer Team matches, including the 2026 SheBelieves Cup. Upcoming installments of The Match, a premier live golf event. Note MLB post-season games are not available in American Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the Northern Mariana Islands. How do I know what games will be on HBO Max?In HBO Max, choose Sports (top of screen or left edge on TVs). Here you'll find live and upcoming games. You can also find games scheduled for the next 2 weeks using our Digital Assistant Sports Schedule. Do I have to pay more for live sports?Live Sports on HBO Max is included with the Standard and Premium plans. Plan availability varies by subscription provider. For more info, go to HBO Max plans. Are there blackout restrictions?Yes. Depending on your location, you won't be able to stream some live games due to league blackout policies. For more info, go to HBO Max blackout restrictions or to find out where the event is being broadcast in your area, check your local listings. How do I watch live sports? In HBO Max, choose Sports (top of the screen or left edge on TVs) and then choose the game you want to watch. Choose Watch Live to start watching the game in progress or Watch from Start to start watching at the beginning. Share location: If you're watching on your phone or tablet, you'll need to share your location with HBO Max. To do this, choose a live game and then share your location when prompted. For more info, go to HBO Max blackout restrictions. Player controls: When watching a live event you can pause, fast forward, rewind, and jump to what's happening live (Go Live button). For more info, go to HBO Max player controls. Devices: Live Sports can be streamed on any supported device. Depending on your device, you can watch live sports in up to HD 1080p with SDR and Dolby Atmos audio. You can also use Chromecast, AirPlay, or an HDMI cable to watch live sports on your TV. Quality: Depending on your device, you can watch live sports in up to HD 1080p with SDR and Dolby Atmos audio. Select events are available in HDR10 or Dolby Vision. If the screen appears too dark, go to Watch in HDR & Dolby Vision. Replays: Replays are available for NHL games, cycling events, March Madness®, and U.S. Men’s and Women's National Soccer Team matches. Captions: To turn closed captions on or off, choose the Audio and Subtitles icon in the video player. Closed captions for live sports are available in English and are slightly delayed. To find out how to change the caption styling (e.g. font and size), go to Subtitles, captions, and audio. Note Closed captions are currently not available for live cycling events. Ads: Live sports events include ads. Live sports from TBS, TNT, and truTV have the same commercials that air during the TV broadcast of the event. Some sports (e.g., cycling events) may have ads before the sports event starts. Alerts: Alerts let you know about key moments in related sports events—for example, when a goal is scored. Choose the alert to start watching the other event. Select the Alerts icon (upper right) in the video player to turn alerts on or off. Some NASCAR and Roland-Garros events have multiple live streams on the same screen at once: Multiview. Things to know about Multiview: Multiview: To watch more action on one screen, choose a pre-set Multiview stream (go to Sports and choose a live sport with Multiview). Supported devices: Multiview is available on phones, tablets, computers, and TV devices. Change focus: Use the directional buttons on your TV remote (or computer keyboard) to switch between views. Audio: By default, audio plays for the top-left view. Computer and TV device: When you change the focus, the audio changes to the focused view. Phone and tablet: Open the Audio and Subtitles menu and choose one of the available options. Full screen: Switch the focus to the view you want to expand, then press the select button on your TV remote (Enter on your computer keyboard) to enter Full screen. To return to the Multiview stream, press the back button. Expanding Multiview to full screen is not available on phones and tablets. Captions: Captions appear at the bottom of the screen for the focused view. To turn captions on or off, enter Full screen, choose the Audio and Subtitles icon , then choose English – CC or Off. For more info, go to Subtitles, captions, and audio. Captions are not available in Multiview on phones and tablets. If you can't see captions while watching in Multiview, try updating your HBO Max app to the latest version. For help, go to Install HBO Max on supported devices and choose your device. Note You can't change what appears in the pre-set Multiviews. Can I also watch Bleacher Report content using my HBO Max account? With Sports on HBO Max, you can also watch video coverage on the Bleacher Report app or website. To do this, sign in to Bleacher Report with your HBO Max account credentials. Here's how: Open the B/R app on your phone or tablet, or go to bleacherreport.com on your computer. Start watching a live event. When prompted, choose Sign in to TV Provider. Choose View All Providers. Scroll down and choose HBO Max. Sign in with your HBO Max email and password and then choose Done. What's new with HBO Max?
